facts.t: Over 1.8 crore cases are stuck before they even begin
facts.d: They sit at the appearance or service-of-summons stage — no evidence, no argument, no adjudication. Roughly a third of the district-court backlog is a postal and process problem rather than a judicial one.

facts.t: The government is the biggest litigant in India
facts.d: The State is a party in about half of all pending cases. Departments routinely appeal rather than settle, because no official is penalised for appealing and every official is exposed for withdrawing.

facts.t: India has 21 judges per million people
facts.d: The Law Commission and the Malimath Committee both recommended 50 per million. More than 180,000 cases have now been pending for over thirty years — longer than many of the litigants have been adults.

bank.q: Approximately what share of India's total pendency sits in district and subordinate courts?
bank.e: Roughly 85 to 87% — around 4.5 to 4.9 crore of the 5.5 crore total. High Courts hold 11 to 13% and the Supreme Court about 0.2%.

bank.q: With reference to the composition of the backlog, consider the following statements:
s: At the subordinate level roughly 77% of cases are criminal.
In the Supreme Court roughly 79% are civil.
Land and property disputes account for about 66% of pending civil cases.
bank.e: All three are correct. The criminal-civil ratio inverts as one moves up the hierarchy.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Supreme Court's sanctioned strength was raised from 34 to 38
The judge-to-population ratio meets the Law Commission benchmark
More than 180,000 cases have been pending for over thirty years
bank.e: India stands at around 21 judges per million against a benchmark of 50 — less than half.

bank.q: Match List I (country) with List II (mechanism India could draw on):
pairs: 1. Court-annexed mediation built into civil procedure before trial
2. Judges fixing trial timelines at the first hearing
3. Statutory deadlines for categories of cases, centrally monitored
4. High judge ratio with written procedure to shorten hearings
bank.e: Singapore's judicial case management, American court-annexed ADR, Germany's staffing and written procedure, and the time-bound disposal targets of Rwanda and South Korea.

bank.as: Article 136 is cited as a cause of Supreme Court congestion.
bank.rs: Special leave has expanded far beyond an exceptional remedy, turning the Court into a routine court of appeal.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — which is why restraining expansive SLP admission features in every reform list.

bank.q: Consider the following measures taken in 2026:
s: Four Special Division Benches were constituted for roughly 800 legacy cases.
A unified digital case-status platform linking all three tiers went live.
The AI Committee was reconstituted under Justice P. S. Narasimha.
bank.e: All three are correct, alongside the advance-transfer policy for Chief Justices designate.

bank.q: Plea bargaining in India is used in what proportion of cases, against the continental European range?
bank.e: Under 1% in India against 15 to 30% in continental Europe — the largest untapped capacity in the criminal justice system.

bank.q: All of the following are structural causes of pendency in the lower judiciary EXCEPT:
o: Delays in investigation and forensic reporting
Multiplicity of parallel civil and criminal proceedings
bank.e: The Constitution Bench backlog is a higher-judiciary problem — though it does stall subordinate proceedings awaiting authoritative rulings.

bank.q: The Union Budget 2026–27 allocation for judicial infrastructure and e-Courts was:
bank.e: ₹2,010 crore in total — ₹810 crore for district infrastructure and ₹1,200 crore for e-Courts Phase III. The ₹7,210 crore figure is the full Phase III outlay across 2023 to 2027.

bank.q: With reference to proposed reforms, consider the following:
s: A binding three-to-six-month timeline between collegium recommendation and notification.
Reviving the All-India Judicial Service with safeguards for state autonomy.
Abolishing Article 136 to end the appeals flood.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are proposed. The recommendation on Article 136 is restraint in admitting special leave petitions, not abolition of the jurisdiction.

bank.q: Undertrial review is now governed by which provision?
bank.e: Section 479 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, which replaced section 436A of the old Code.

bank.as: Technology is described as a servant of justice rather than its substitute.
bank.rs: Artificial intelligence is proposed for allocation, cause lists, translation and research, but not for adjudication.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the boundary the reconstituted AI Committee is expected to police.
